rationale: The conditioning leg is essentially the published net-external-financing / composite-issuance anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan, Daniel-Titman) and, within this archive, a mechanical dollar sum of the two already-tested legs (CheapDeleveragingFromProfits and CheapSelfFundedEquityBase) that debt flows will numerically dominate, so it is closer to a repackaging than a new mechanism.

This is a denominator swap on the immediately preceding proposal, and deflating the financing flow by market cap puts 1/price in both the gate and the signal, so any measured edge is partly a mechanical value/size repackaging rather than evidence about the financing channel.

The timing-of-credit-repricing channel is a legitimate extension of the archive's cross-market idea, but DELTA(xint/debt) falls mechanically when debt is raised late in the fiscal year, so the computed quantity is heavily contaminated by debt issuance — the very thing the archive's deleveraging signal treats with the opposite sign.

A sign-flipped gate on the same construction as proposal 1, testing what is already well documented — that issuance and asset-growth/external-finance effects are concentrated in high-multiple firms — and it overlaps heavily with FF5's CMA and the share-issuance anomaly.

Besides being a re-run of the already-diluted level-plus-flow fusion with a different deflator, the flow leg drops COALESCE(dvc,0) so DELTA(ceq)-ib mixes payout into "external finance abstinence," directly contradicting the reconciliation the same batch used to justify including dividends.

Debt maturity structure is a genuinely distinct, FF5-orthogonal channel not represented anywhere in the archive, though the ratio is unstable for firms with trivial total debt (all-current-maturity micro-balances score as extreme rollover risk) and the WINSOR on an already-bounded ratio is inert, so an interaction with leverage level would sharpen it.
